blocks.text: Instruction following fine-tuning teaches a base model, which by default only predicts plausible text continuations, to instead interpret an instruction and produce a response that actually carries out what was asked, the foundational capability that makes a model usable as an assistant at all.

This topic covers what distinguishes instruction tuning data from the narrower task-specific fine-tuning covered elsewhere in this module, and why diversity of instruction types matters for a model to generalize well.
1. From Raw Completion to Following Instructions

blocks.alt: From Raw Completion to Following Instructions
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614634-390476844.png

A base pretrained model, left as is, simply continues text in a statistically plausible way, given the instruction "summarize this article" it might continue with more instructions rather than an actual summary, instruction tuning specifically teaches the model to recognize an instruction and act on it.
2. The Instruction-Input-Output Data Shape
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614635-631882158.png

Instruction tuning datasets typically structure each example as an instruction describing the task, an optional input the instruction operates on, and the expected output demonstrating the correct response, a data shape covered in more general terms in the earlier Supervised Fine-Tuning module.
3. Why Diversity of Instructions Matters
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614635-182834020.png

Unlike the narrower task-specific fine-tuning covered later in this module, summarization or classification alone, instruction tuning deliberately spans many different instruction types, summarizing, translating, explaining, writing, so the model learns the general skill of interpreting and acting on an instruction rather than memorizing one narrow behavior.
4. Covering a Wide Range of Instruction Verbs

blocks.alt: Covering a Wide Range of Instruction Verbs
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614885-756982482.png

A well constructed instruction tuning dataset covers many different instruction verbs and phrasings, this variety is what teaches the model the general pattern of instruction following rather than a narrow set of memorized instruction templates.

blocks.text: 5. Generalizing to Unseen Instructions
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614887-991792688.png

A key goal of instruction tuning is generalization, a model trained on a diverse enough set of instructions should be able to reasonably follow a new instruction phrasing it never saw during training, this generalization is what separates genuine instruction following from simple memorization.

blocks.title: Generalization is the real measure of instruction tuning quality
blocks.content: Testing a model on instructions deliberately excluded from training, sometimes called held out instruction evaluation, is the most direct way to check whether instruction tuning actually generalized rather than just memorized the training set.

blocks.text: 6. Instruction Tuning as the First Stage

blocks.alt: Instruction Tuning as the First Stage
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614888-870099292.png

Instruction tuning is typically the first fine-tuning stage a base model goes through, establishing basic instruction following ability before a preference optimization stage, RLHF, DPO, or the other methods covered in the earlier Alignment Training module, further refines response quality and alignment with human preferences.
7. Handling Ambiguous Instructions
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472614889-525747853.png

Real instructions are sometimes ambiguous or underspecified, training data that includes examples of reasonable handling, either asking a clarifying follow up question or making a sensible default assumption and stating it, teaches the model to handle this realistic case rather than only ever seeing perfectly specified instructions.
8. Instruction Tuning vs Chat Models

Instruction tuning as covered here typically focuses on single-turn instruction and response pairs, chat models, covered in the next topic, extend this same underlying idea to multi-turn conversations where context accumulates across several exchanges.
9. Data Sources for Instruction Tuning

Instruction tuning datasets are commonly built from a mix of human-written examples, existing task datasets reformatted into instruction shape, and model-generated examples that are then filtered or reviewed, covered more generally in the earlier Dataset Preparation module.
Worked Example

A team fine-tuning a general purpose assistant collects instruction tuning data spanning summarization, explanation, rewriting, and question answering instructions, deliberately varying phrasing across examples of the same underlying task type.

After training, they test the model on a held out set of instructions using verbs and phrasings that never appeared during training, confirming the model generalizes reasonably well rather than only handling instructions that closely match its training examples, before moving on to a preference optimization stage.
Common Mistakes

items: Using narrow, repetitive instruction phrasing that teaches memorization rather than genuine generalization
Skipping instruction tuning and going straight to preference optimization on a model that cannot yet follow basic instructions
Not testing on held out, unseen instruction phrasings to actually verify generalization
Confusing instruction tuning data, single-turn instruction and response, with the multi-turn data chat models need

blocks.text: Practice

Write five instruction tuning examples spanning at least three different instruction verbs, summarize, explain, rewrite, or similar, then write one held out test instruction using a verb not covered in your five examples, and reason through whether your training set would likely generalize to it.
Key Takeaway

Instruction following fine-tuning teaches a base completion model to interpret and act on varied instructions rather than simply continuing text, using a diverse instruction-input-output dataset that prioritizes generalization to unseen phrasings, forming the foundational first stage most fine-tuning pipelines build alignment training on top of.
